articleTitle: Bee Colony-Reptile Search Optimization Technique for Blood Cell Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: The biosystem is a crucial system grounded in classification and detection, utilizing Artificial Intelligence (AI) approaches or metaheuristic techniques. Currently, cancer of the blood cells is among the deadliest cancers in the world. Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) is a cancer of blood cells that causes excessive proliferation of lymphocytes. It is extremely time-consuming and expensive to conduct diagnostic calculations. The number of platelets in a patient's blood is computed by a platelet count. A lacking number of platelets can indicate cancer, infection, or other health problems. A patient with too many platelets is at risk for blood strokes. A single drop of blood includes tens of thousands of platelets. The main goal of this paper is how to detect the features of blood cells and classify with predicting cancer type based on platelets analysis by using Bee Colony followed by Reptile Search Optimization (BCRSO) technique. According to the results, BCRSO algorithm performed better in terms of classification efficacy and accuracy rate than other algorithms. Based on simulation results, the proposed method is more effective than previously published research for classification optimization.

articleTitle: Self-Organization of Wireless Sensor Networks for Wildfire Detection Using Shapley Values
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Wildfires have devastating impacts on the environment, economy and public health. Early detection can help mitigate damage but detection can be challenging in remote and inaccessible areas. Wireless sensor networks provide an effective solution. These networks consist of inexpensive nodes that monitor the environment and transmit the sensed data over wireless links to a base state. Sensor nodes are usually randomly distributed via air and must self-organize to create the network. This paper proposes a new self-organizing method that forms a hierarchical sensor network suitable for wildfire detection. Clusters are formed without a predefined structure or the need for localization. Shapley values are used to select cluster heads as new clusters are dynamically created during self-organization. Routing paths for aggregated data are naturally defined as clusters are created. Simulation results are presented to show the effectiveness of this approach.

articleTitle: Adaptive Admittance Control for Collaborative Assembly Using Dual Parallel-Serial Robots
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: The admittance control is currently an effective method for enabling robots to perceive external environments, adapt to complex assembly conditions, and furtherly achieve satisfactory compliant assembly. Aiming at the limitations of serial robots with insufficient load capacities, this paper puts forward an asymmetrical multi-robot assembly solution based on dual parallel-serial robots. This system integrates the complementary advantages of different robots, effectively resolving the conflict between precision and flexibility. Focusing on the ability to assembly with compliance of this parallel-serial robots system, a fuzzy adaptive admittance control strategy for typical assembly scenarios is proposed. This strategy incorporates an adaptive update function utilizing fuzzy inference and an improved hyperbolic tangent function for adjusting the damping parameters. Eventually, the effectiveness of this method is verified through peg-hole assembly experiment on a prototype.

articleTitle: Effect of Industrial Robot Load on its Pose Repeatability and Working Cycle Time
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: The experiments presented in this paper aim to assess the effect of proper loading of the end of the robot's arm on its pose repeatability and working cycle time. The measurement is carried out on a FANUC LR Mate 200iC industrial robot using a digital indicator. The experiment was carried out at five different robot loads. For each single load, a measurement in three axes was performed. The experiment also includes an assessment of the influence of the detailed definition of the end of the robot's arm load in its control system on the measurement results. The paper provides insight into the possibility of investigating the performance criteria of industrial robots and highlights the essence of the correct setting of the robot load including the moments of inertia and the position of the center of gravity.

articleTitle: Anomaly Detection System for Possible Cheating During Online Examination
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Online exams are vulnerable to cheating due to the absence of direct supervision. This study uses webcams to present a system for detecting smartphone use and off-screen gaze during online exams. Leveraging YOLOv8 for smartphone and face detection and MediaPipe for head pose estimation, the system analyzes live web cam feeds in real-time anomaly detection. We trained the system using a merged dataset derived from public Roboflow datasets. The system achieved high accuracy, with a mean average precision (mAP@O.5) of 97.9% for smartphones and 99.5% for faces. Head pose estimation demonstrated low mean absolute errors (MAE). This integrated approach enhances academic integrity in online assessments, providing a real-time monitoring tool for educators.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Design and Taguchi Method Optimization of High-Speed Permanent Magnet Motors for Air Compressors
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Hydrogen fuel cell vehicles have a significant effect on reducing carbon emissions in the automotive industry. In the hydrogen fuel cell system, the air compressor, due to its unique high-speed requirements, must rely on a specially designed highspeed motor to provide the necessary driving force. The highspeed nature of the motor presents unprecedented challenges to key performance aspects such as efficiency and operational stability. This paper focuses on the design of a high-efficiency permanent magnet high-speed synchronous motor with low cogging torque, suitable for hydrogen fuel cell vehicles. It includes an analysis of motor size design, comparison of magnetization methods, and optimization using the Taguchi method. The findings are of practical significance for the optimization of highspeed permanent magnet synchronous motors and for the development of hydrogen fuel cell vehicles.

articleTitle: Two Decades of Progress in Deep Learning for Drive Failure Prediction (2004-2024): A Bibliometric Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: This paper systematically analyzes research trends, hotspots, and collaboration patterns in the application of Deep Learning (DL) for Drive Failure Prediction (DFP) through a scientometric approach. By examining relevant literature from major academic databases over the past two decades, it identifies leading authors, institutions, and countries/region contributing to the field. Furthermore, the paper explores the evolution of research themes and academic interests using co-occurrence network analysis. The findings reveal a significant increase in DLdriven predictive maintenance research, with growing interest in enhancing prediction accuracy and operational efficiency. This study provides valuable insights for researchers and practitioners aiming to advance the field of drive failure prediction through DL technologies.

articleTitle: Developing Multi-Factor Authentication and Biometric Verification Protocols for Enhancing Data Security in IoT Healthcare Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: This paper introduces a Multi-Factor Authentication System for enhancing data security in IoT healthcare devices. The system comprises the Multi-Factor Authentication Algorithm (MFAA), Biometric Template Protection Algorithm (BTPA), Dynamic Risk-Based Authentication Algorithm (DRBAA), Adaptive Biometric Fusion Algorithm (ABFA), and Context-Aware Access Control Algorithm (CAACA). Through a comparative analysis, the proposed system consistently outperforms existing methods, demonstrating its potential for robust, context-aware, and adaptive user authentication. The ablation study delves into the individual contributions of each algorithm, emphasizing their collective strength in creating a secure and versatile authentication framework. The proposed system stands as a promising solution for addressing the evolving challenges of data security in the dynamic landscape of IoT healthcare.

articleTitle: Analysis the Effect of Listening Music on the Human Brain by Using Electroencephalogram (EEG) Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: This research investigates the impact of music reflexology on brain activity, utilizing Electroencephalogram (EEG) features to analyze neurological responses. The study addresses two primary objectives: Identifying the effectiveness of music listening on humans and analyzing the relationship between different signals released by the different activity and music reflexology using EEG feature (Alpha, Beta, and Theta Bands). EEG data were collected from various subjects during induced stress (Cognitive task English comprehension test) and listening to the music in the reflexology sessions. EEG signal comparisons across various activities reveal that stress or cognitive demands increase Beta wave activity while decreasing Alpha and Theta waves. Conversely, relaxing activities like listening to calming music increase Alpha and Theta waves and reduce Beta waves. In conclusion, music significantly influences human emotions and physiological states, particularly through compositions with slow tempos, harmonic structures, and acoustic instruments that enhance relaxation and reduce stress.

articleTitle: Classification of Alcoholic Beverage Using Electronic Nose and Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: In recent years, machine learning algorithms have seen significant development and implementation within the technological industry as ways to optimize training data and classification. The study aims to make use of an electronic nose system that is designed to classify five types of alcoholic beverages. Beer, gin, red wine, whiskey, and rum by using their distinct gas signatures. The system uses a Raspberry Pi 4 microcontroller, integrated with MQ gas sensors (MQ-2, MQ-3, MQ-4, MQ-7, and MQ-135) to detect ethanol, carbon dioxide. And other distinct compounds that are emitted by the beverages. A Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithm was implemented to analyze and classify the data gathered from the sensors. By using 100 trials with 20 samples for each beverage, were used in training and evaluating the model. The results yielded an overall classification accuracy of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{9 0 \%}$</tex> which was verified by a confusion matrix. The findings demonstrate the potential of the system to identify between different alcoholic beverage types with precision which may have a potential application in quality control and alcoholic beverage authentication.

articleTitle: Verifying Pid Controller of Robot Car by Deltareachability Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Verifying the safety of cyber-physical systems is widely recognized as an important concern, especially the safety of autonomous driving systems. In this paper, we focus on the PID controller of a robot car and verify its safety requirements. The verification of such systems is done through reachability analysis. However, this problem is undecidable. Therefore, we check the socalled delta-reachability, which is a weaker notion of reachability, to verify the safety requirements. We model the car as a hybrid system and utilize a delta-reachability solver for verification. Several combinations of PID gains are tested and evaluated.

articleTitle: An AI-Enabled Centralized Monitoring System to Predict SME Inventory Level
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Adapting to the fast changes of the market along with the dynamic environment and customer demand, creates a very competitive marketplace for small and medium enterprises (SMEs). Such a technology-driven market requires impulsive and viable action to enable the service providers to stay on track and follow the flow. It is very important to know the market demand and movement, which are not monthly but daily and are responses to the immediate demand. Artificial intelligence enables SMEs to observe the market demand, record the movement, and learn from it. Continuous tracking and learning of changes will enable the machine to predict upcoming patterns. This is helpful as it enables service providers to know what product or service is in demand for each specific month and even further for each specific week and day based on cumulated data and then be prepared for it. This paper proposes an AI-enabled centralized monitoring system to help SMEs observe, track, and predict upcoming market demands. The system uses hybrid learning with the help of historical data to come up with a trend and prediction following the observation of customer behavior.

articleTitle: Classification and Detection for Oryza Folia (Palay Leaf) Disease an Analysis with YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: This study demonstrated the effectiveness of the YOLOv5 object detection model in automating the classification and detection of six common diseases affecting the Palay (rice) leaves using advanced machine learning techniques, the model was able to reliably diagnose diseases from leaf images, addressing an important problem in agricultural production. The image classification model training progresses through 30 epochs and shows significant improvement in its performance on the training model as it reaches 0.989 or 98% accuracy at the end of the training. The classification result for bacterial blight that is predominant in the subject oryza folia was successfully classified by the model. This can also be compared visually to accurately having 50% bacterial blight, also based on the model's performance as the accuracy yield starting at 36.1% to 98% in image classification. The system model allows for early intervention and mitigation strategies, reducing potential yield losses due to crop diseases.

articleTitle: A Review of Evolutionary Algorithms for Integrated Healthcare Scheduling Problems
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: This review explores the use of evolutionary algorithms in integrated healthcare scheduling, focusing on nurse and operation theatre scheduling. While various optimization methods are discussed, there is a notable gap in applying evolutionary algorithms. The study highlights the potential of Cooperative Co-Evolutionary Algorithms (CCEAs) to address complex scheduling challenges, including resource constraints and service integration. CCEAs are promising due to their adaptability and scalability. The review calls for more research and empirical validation to improve efficiency and patient care in integrated healthcare scheduling.

articleTitle: An Attention-Based Generative Adversarial Network for Limited-Angle CT Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Reconstructing high-quality computed tomography (CT) images from limited-angle projections is a challenging and ill-posed problem, often resulting in severe artifacts and loss of structural details. Traditional analytical methods, such as Filtered Back Projection (FBP), struggle with incomplete data, while existing deep learning approaches face limitations in generalization and reliance on extensive paired datasets. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)-based framework comprising a U-Net-inspired generator enhanced with residual blocks and selfattention mechanisms, coupled with a PatchGAN discriminator. The generator effectively captures long-range dependencies and structural features critical for artifact removal and reconstruction accuracy, while the PatchGAN discriminator enforces local texture realism. Additionally, a perceptual loss derived from a pretrained VGG network preserves fine anatomical details and high-level semantic consistency. Extensive evaluations on clinical datasets demonstrate the superiority of our method over state-of-the-art techniques. Quantitative metrics, including PSNR, SSIM, and MSE, confirm significant improvements, and qualitative results showcase the effective suppression of artifacts and recovery of fine structural details.

articleTitle: Lip-Reading for Philippine Regional Language Classification of Cebuano and Ilocano
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Automated lip-reading systems face significant challenges in multilingual environments, particularly in the Philippines, where dialects such as Cebuano and Ilocano have distinct phonetic-visual attributes. Existing methods mostly rely on audio and visual fusion for processing, while others, such as LipNet and LCSNet, focus on visual-only techniques using 3D Convolutional Neural Networks (3D CNN), Bidirectional LongShort Term Memory (BiLSTM), and Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC). Although these systems have achieved excellent performance, such as LipNet with a 95.2 % accuracy, they lack the capability to classify multiple languages. This study introduces a lip-reading model inspired by LipNet and LCSNet that not only performs word-for-word prediction but also distinguishes between the Cebuano and Ilocano dialects. Data was gathered from 2000 videos of samples articulating lexicons in these languages, which were then evaluated using one general confusion matrix for the regional language classification gathering an accuracy of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{8 8 \%}$</tex>. Another two <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10 \times 10$</tex> confusion matrices were also used to on measuring the accuracy of lexiconlevel classification resulting to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{6 4 \%}$</tex> for Cebuano and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{5 8 \%}$</tex> for Ilocano.

articleTitle: Advancing Structural Safety: Genetic Programming Approaches to Steel Fiber-Reinforced Concrete (SFRC) Blast Response Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Steel Fiber-Reinforced Concrete (SFRC) has emerged as a preferred material for blast-resistant structures due to its exceptional mechanical properties and energy absorption capabilities. This study introduces a machine learning-based framework to predict the maximum displacement of SFRC structural members under blast loading. Using 107 experimental data points, split into <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{7 0 \%}$</tex> for training and 15 % each for validation and testing, Gene Expression Programming (GEP) and Multi-Expression Programming (MEP) were applied. The GEP model exhibited superior predictive performance with R -values of 0.964 (training), 0.968 (validation), and 0.960 (testing), while the MEP model achieved reasonable accuracy with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex>-values of 0.922, 0.905, and 0.948, respectively. Additionally, parametric analysis revealed the influence of fiber properties on SFRC behavior. This approach not only simplifies predictive modeling but also enhances its reliability, offering valuable insights for optimizing SFRC design under extreme conditions and contributing to the advancement of resilient structural systems.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Impact of Weather on Dynamic Ordering Through XAI
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: The objectives of this study are to optimize delivery strategies and estimate CO2 emission reductions. The results of the analysis showed, first, that the Gradient Boosting model is optimal for predicting same-day demand incorporating weather data. Second, it was quantitatively shown that the choice of delivery method based on the clustering results contributes to environmental impact reduction. The novelty of this study is the use of XAI to improve the transparency of the model and incorporate external environmental factors into the delivery planning. It is hoped that the selection of dynamic modeling and delivery methods will lead to a better society.

articleTitle: Neural Networks for Detection and Classification of Open Circuit Faults in Electrical Multiphase Drives
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Multiphase electrical drives are well-known for their high reliability thanks to a higher number of phases compared to three-phase ones. In the event of a fault, multiphase drives can offer a reconfiguration of the control strategy to achieve an acceptable performance. However, reconfiguring the control requires precise information related to the fault location. With an increased number of phases, it becomes necessary to develop new algorithms for fault detection and localization that exploit the unique properties multiphase drives, which differ from those of three-phase drives. This work aims to develop a fault detection and localization method using neural networks for open-phase faults in a five-phase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine (PMSM). To accelerate and simplify the training process, the Hilbert transform is proposed to extract instantaneous phases of currents in the Secondary Machine of a 5 -phase PMSM. Simulation results are presented to confirm the proposed approach.

articleTitle: A Multi-Gpu Edge Server-Based Uav Trajectory Optimization for Emergencies and Disasters
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: This paper investigates the utilization of powerful edge computing servers to significantly reduce the computation time needed to calculate the optimal unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) trajectory. This is especially important for UAVs in order to assist authorities and first responders reach the large number of geographically distributed users who need help during emergencies and disasters. In such hard circumstances, UAVs can help in search and rescue, monitoring, delivering supplies, and providing radio access links. The optimized UAV trajectory is computed using the Travelling Salesman Problem (TSP) approach which is NP-hard and imposes computational challenges. Hence, the TSP algorithm computations are intended to be processed in a ground multigraphics processing unit (GPU) server. In this way, both computational delays and energy consumption will be reduced for the UAV especially with the dynamic environment and large number nodes required to be visited in disaster scenarios. The proposed approach is tested via simulations considering a variable number of visited nodes, and a variable number of GPUs on the edge server. Results show a significant improvement in the computation time when multiple GPUs were used compared to the traditional central processing unit (CPU); however, using more GPUs can also lead to a slightly higher computation time compared to fewer GPUs.

articleTitle: Quantitative Evaluation of Vulnerabilities in Adversarial Shadow Attack
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: As automated driving technology gains global attention, adversarial samples (AEs), a vulnerability of deep neural networks (DNNs), pose a significant threat. Among various AEs, adversarial shadow attacks (ASA) are particularly concerning, as they introduce perturbations through shadows in regions that significantly affect explainable AI (XAI) inference, while also emphasizing their reproducibility in real-world scenarios. However, no effective countermeasures for ASA currently exist. Therefore, since ASA is a type of AEs, we conducted a quantitative evaluation of existing AE countermeasures-such as Bit depth reduction, JPEG conversion, and filter-based smoothing-in an attempt to reduce the perturbations caused by ASA. Specifically, we applied these AE countermeasures to ASA and generated protective images. These images were then classified using an image classifier to assess their impact on inference accuracy. For this study, we used the German Traffic Sign Detection Benchmark dataset and ResNet-50. The highest inference success rate observed with Bit depth reduction was 18.93 %, meaning that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{8 1. 0 7 \%}$</tex> of the cases still resulted in incorrect inference despite applying AE countermeasures. These results demonstrate that current AE countermeasures are ineffective against ASA.

articleTitle: Classification of Local Fish Meat Types in the Philippines Using Electronic Nose
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: The study develops an AI-based Electronic Nose (E-nose) system to classify four common Philippine fish species—Bangus (Milkfish), Galunggong, Lapu-Lapu (Grouper), and Tilapia—based on their volatile organic compound (VOC) signatures. The system utilizes an array of MQ gas sensors for data collection, processed by a Raspberry Pi 5 microcontroller. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is applied for dimensionality reduction, and a Support Vector Machine (SVM) is used for classification. A dataset of 300 fish meat samples (75 per species) was split 80–20 for training and testing. Performance evaluation through a confusion matrix showed a high classification accuracy of 98.66%. These results highlight the potential of E-nose technology for fish meat authentication, ensuring food quality and integrity in the Philippines, where seafood is a vital part of the diet and economy. The system's accuracy demonstrates the effectiveness of AI-driven odor classification for seafood products. Future research can expand this classification system by including more fish species and investigating correlations between fish type and freshness decay, further enhancing food safety and quality control measures in the seafood industry.

articleTitle: Utilizing Binary Segmentation to Enhance Object of Interest Details in Images Synthesized Using Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Image synthesis, once considered a distant fantasy, has emerged as a rapidly evolving field, driven by advancements in generative models and computational power. Many researchers in academia and corporations have tackled this problem and achieved impressive results. Among the widely adopted models in this domain is the Generative Adversarial Network (GAN). In this work, we integrate Binary Segmentation with GANs to enhance the quality of the object of interest in generated images. The binary segmentation model guides the generative model to focus on the region of interest within the image rather than the background producing more detailed representations of the target object. Our approach was trained and validated using labeled samples from the well-known CUB dataset. For testing, we generated images corresponding to text descriptions from the dataset. Evaluation of these images demonstrated the effectiveness of our model, achieving a comparable Inception Score of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5.243\pm 0.090$</tex> with significantly fewer training epochs (200 epochs).

articleTitle: Real Time Robotic Label Affixing for Irregular Items Using Low Cost Depth Sensing and Computational Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: In many applications, items are transported on conveyor belts, and it is desirable to attach RFID tags for efficient tracking and tracing. A notable example is luggage handling at airports, where workers manually attach RFID tags to luggage upon unloading from planes to ensure proper tracking for transfers. This manual process is both tedious and time-consuming, often leading to repetitive strain injuries for workers. This paper presents a developed system that automates this process using a robotic arm equipped with a vision system. The system leverages a low-cost depth sensor and operates on a non-GPU machine, making it feasible for edge computing. It employs traditional algorithm designs, including region growing and template matching, providing a deterministic approach to label affixing. By deploying service robots for repetitive tasks such as label affixing, we can reduce human fatigue, mitigate repetitive strain injuries, and save time. This service robot effectively replicates manual label affixing tasks, enhancing efficiency and improving overall workflow in luggage handling.

articleTitle: Improving Delivery Time Predictions Using Real-World Traffic Information and Delivery Performance Data: Enhancing Customer Satisfaction and Enabling Data-Driven Decision-Making
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: This study quantitatively evaluates how improving delivery time prediction accuracy constructed using real-world traffic information impacts economic efficiency through computational simulation. It proposes a practical framework to optimize delivery operations and support data-driven decision-making. The results show that improving delivery time prediction accuracy led to a 2% increase in revenue and a 21% improvement in customer satisfaction, highlighting the economic and operational benefits of integrating real-world traffic information. This indicates that enhancing delivery time prediction accuracy can lead to economic efficiency gains and improved customer experience, enabling businesses to optimize delivery operations and improve competitive advantage. This research strengthens the foundation of data-driven management and provides a practical framework for establishing a competitive advantage.

articleTitle: An Analysis of Gpt-4O's Capability to Detect Incongruity in Double-Bind Scenarios With Text and Images
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: This study evaluates the detection of Incongruity in double-bind scenarios combining text and images, utilizing OpenAI's GPT-4o. The research focuses on three aspects: (1) GPT-4o's capability to detect Incongruity, (2) the impact of image polarity (positive vs. negative impressions) on detection, and (3) alignment between GPT-4o's assessments and human evaluations. Images with both positive and negative valence, along with corresponding texts reflecting similar positive or negative valence, were presented in various combinations. GPT-4o assessed likability, mood, and Incongruity using a 7-point scale. Results indicate that GPT-4o effectively identifies Incongruity in multimodal inputs, with performance closely matching human evaluations. However, inconsistencies were noted in judgment trends influenced by image polarity. Despite these variations, GPT-4o predominantly prioritized textual cues over visual data in detecting Incongruity. These findings highlight the promise of multimodal AI systems in recognizing complex emotional and logical inconsistencies, while also underscoring limitations caused by image-induced biases. Future research should address these limitations by leveraging diverse datasets and real-world scenarios to enhance the robustness and generalizability of such systems.

articleTitle: Design of a Triple-Input, Single-Output Powered Aquaponics System with Iot Battery Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Most aquaponics systems relied only on either a single source or a combination of two to power such systems. It mainly used Solar and Grid Power. The main objective of this paper is to design an Aquaponics System that integrates a TripleInput, Single Output Power Supply with IOT Monitoring. The study focused mostly on the system's power switching capabilities and was limited to the ratings of the components or devices that were used. The researchers have designed and constructed a prototype that provided such function and tested whether the data being displayed were reliable and evaluated whether the environment itself was livable for Tilapia and Lettuce species. After conducting a 30 -day observation period it was seen that the IoT monitoring system produced reliable results for monitored parameters except for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{p H}$</tex> sensor wherein its recorded error percentage was 0.6641 %. The average weekly growth observed for Tilapia was 2.57 grams and 3.071 centimeters for Lettuce. The designed aquaponics system has demonstrated that the TRISO charging on its battery enables continuous operation.

articleTitle: SIGNSPEAK: Integrating Computer Vision and Speech Synthesis for Alphabet Filipino Sign Language (FSL)
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: In our interconnected world, effective communication is a fundamental human right fostering social interaction, education, and personal growth. However, individuals with sensory impairments, such as hearing loss, encounter significant barriers in communication, hindering their participation in society. This challenge is pronounced in the Philippines, where Filipino Sign Language (FSL) is vital for the Deaf community. The “SignSpeak” study addresses these challenges by integrating computer vision and speech synthesis technologies. Utilizing platforms like Raspberry Pi and Jetson Nano, SignSpeak interprets hand gestures in real-time, converting them into audible speech, and translates spoken language into text, enabling bidirectional communication. This approach empowers individuals with varying sensory abilities, fostering inclusivity and enhancing educational opportunities. SignSpeak promotes social equity and empowers the Deaf community in the Philippines through rigorous software and hardware development and a commitment to linguistic inclusivity. Beyond technical innovations, SignSpeak envisions a future where individuals of all abilities can communicate freely and participate in society. The study results were highly successful, demonstrating 95% accuracy, 96% precision, 94% recall, and a 95% F1 score. Additionally, the prototype received positive feedback, with an overall mean score of 4.845. These outcomes highlight SignSpeak's effectiveness and potential impact in improving communication accessibility for the Deaf community in the Philippines.

articleTitle: Iot-Based Mobile Application of Three-Phase Induction Motors Monitoring and Fault Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Induction motors have become the most used motors in industrial applications in recent years. However, despite their high reliability, operating conditions can expose induction motors to various fault conditions. Implementing condition monitoring is crucial to prevent unexpected motor shutdowns and enhance the motor's productivity and lifespan. One effective approach to monitoring is leveraging the Internet of Things (IoT), which enables real-time data collection, data visualization through graphs, and the development of web services and connections. The objective of this research is to monitor real-time data and detect electrical faults in a three-phase induction motor. The monitored electrical parameters include voltage, current, and temperature. The system will identify faults such as overcurrent, overvoltage, undervoltage, undercurrent, and overtemperature. Once a fault is detected, the system will isolate the motor to prevent further damage. Additionally, the system will utilize the Internet of Things to measure and display electrical parameters, including voltage, current, and temperature, along with their corresponding graphs, through a mobile application. Data transmission between the system and the mobile application will occur between 7-8 a.m. and 9-10 p.m. The mobile application will access a history log, allowing users to review past data. Furthermore, the application will compile information about motor faults that occurred on specific days and times, which will be displayed in the error logs.

articleTitle: Optimizing Fruit Yield Prediction: Evaluating Multiobject Tracking Algorithms for Calamansi Fruit Detection Using Yolov8m
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Accurate fruit yield prediction is necessary for enhancing agricultural methods and providing quality output. This work analyzes the efficacy of multi-object tracking (MOT) algorithms in detecting calamansi fruits from drone-captured video footage, using the YOLOv8m object detection model. Data were gathered from a commercial calamansi farm in Naujan, Philippines, and prepared for model training. Three MOT algorithms-SORT, DeepSORT, and ByteTrack-were evaluated using performance metrics such as Multiple Object Tracking Accuracy (MOTA), Higher Order Tracking Accuracy (HOTA), and ID F1 Score (IDF1). ByteTrack achieved exceptional performance with MOTA, HOTA, and IDF1 ratings of 59.67 %, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{6 5. 4 2 \%}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{7 3. 7 2 \%}$</tex> respectively. The integration of YOLOv8m for detection with ByteTrack for tracking significantly reduced double-counting while ensuring good computational efficiency. The results underscore ByteTrack's capability in real-time fruit monitoring and its significance for improving yield estimate and agricultural production.

articleTitle: Automated Library Shelf Management System with Programmable Logic Controller and Human-machine Interface
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: This paper explores the shelf movement in a library system, driven by an Allen-Bradley PLC and an HMI interface. This project was part of the advanced PLC course at Michigan Technological University and involved building a prototype of library shelves using 3D printing technology. The system is controlled by a PLC, which manages NEMA stepper motors and motor drivers to facilitate shelf movement. Limit switches are employed to ensure the safe positioning of the shelves, preventing them from crashing into the walls, while a photoelectric sensor provides additional safety by ensuring the shelves do not move towards a person. This project demonstrates the integration of advanced control systems and mechanical design to automate library shelf operations efficiently.

articleTitle: Student Posture Extraction and Attentiveness Classification Using Deeplabcut and Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: This study proposes a computer vision system to classify student attentiveness in physical classrooms using upperbody posture analysis. Leveraging the DeepLabCut framework for pose estimation and a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier, the system processes video data captured via a Raspberry Pi 5 and an OBSBot Tail Air camera to categorize attentiveness into three levels: fully attentive, partially attentive, and nonattentive. Unlike existing methods focused on online learning environments, this approach targets physical classroom settings, addressing gaps in engagement monitoring. The model was trained on annotated posture data from volunteers, with body part coordinates normalized relative to the thorax for consistency. Evaluation using a confusion matrix revealed an accuracy of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{7 0. 8 5 \%}$</tex>, highlighting challenges in distinguishing subtle posture variations between attentiveness levels. The system provides instructors with actionable insights to adapt teaching strategies, promoting personalized learning. This work demonstrates the feasibility of integrating low-cost hardware and machine learning for classroom engagement analytics, though future studies could benefit from larger datasets and enhanced classification models.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor State Prediction Using Image Segmentation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Due to the incidence of brain tumors-both slow-growing and fast-growing types-occurring at approximately 18.71 cases per 100,000 people worldwide, their significance has become increasingly apparent. Fast-growing tumors, in particular, complicate treatment, increase risks, and adversely affect both physical and mental health while raising mortality rates. Therefore, this thesis focuses on developing a program for brain tumor staging classification using deep learning technology. The Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture was chosen as the primary model due to its high efficiency in processing medical images and relatively short training time. The developed system was trained and tested using an MRI brain tumor image dataset, divided into training, validation, and testing sets. Experimental results showed that the model achieved a mean IoU (Intersection over Union) score of 0.885, indicating the overlap between the model's output and the ground truth, and a classification accuracy of 98.71 % for brain tumor staging (averaged across all classes).

articleTitle: Evaluating Deep Learning Methods for Virtual Sensors in Water Infrastructure Digital Twins
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Water scarcity is an increasing global issue, with the demand for water potentially exceeding supply, and organizations failing to balance current and future needs. Continuous monitoring and accurate prediction of water availability, proactive leakage detection and optimising water consumption are crucial, necessitating advanced, cost-effective, and highly accurate methods for effective water management. The integration of the Internet of Things (IoT) with Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Industry 4.0 has significantly enhanced monitoring, automated industrial processes and enabled forecasting. High-quality data is essential to deliver precise insights and optimal performance. Virtual sensors, which digitally replicate failed IoT sensors, offer a smart solution for data generation, that impacts water infrastructure monitoring. This study employs deep learning models Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Variational Autoencoders (VAE), to generate synthetic data for virtual sensors. The findings indicate that LSTM provide better outputs, paving the way for further development and implementation of virtual sensors in Water Infrastructure Digital Twins.

articleTitle: Investigation of Anytime Evolutionary DCOP Algorithm on Pub/Sub Communication Platform with Message Losses
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Distributed constraint optimization problems (DCOPs) have been studied as a fundamental framework for cooperative problem solving in multiagent systems, including distributed resource allocation and collaborative tasks. With a DCOP, a cooperation task is represented as a constraint optimization problem distributed among agents, and a decentralized optimization algorithm is applied to find its optimal solution. Although several studies have addressed extended problems toward practical implementations, opportunities exist to investigate the implementation techniques of the solution methods on dedicated platforms for different devices. Several recent platforms for robots and communication infrastructures for IoT devices employ a publish/subscribe communication model. Toward the application of distributed constraint optimization methods to the cooperation of edge devices on such platforms/infrastructures, solution methods for dedicated communication models must be explored. Previous studies investigated an implementation methodology of the case of the maximum gain message (MGM) algorithm, which is the simplest local search method, on a pub/sub communication platform with message losses under best-effort settings. However, further investigation and typification for different types of solution methods are necessary to extend this approach. As the next step of this research direction, we investigate the case of the Anytime Evolutionary DCOP (AED) algorithm and verify its actual implementation in a similar ROS2 environment. The contribution of this study is summarized as follows. (1) We present a version of the AED algorithm for the implementation on pub/sub communication platforms. (2) We modify the AED on pub/sub communication so that the solution process continues under the situations with temporarily missing agents. (3) We implement the proposed method on an actual platform of an ROS2 environment and experimentally verify its effect. (4) We experimentally compare the proposed method with the MGM algorithm implemented on the same actual environment and present promising solution quality with the proposed approach in convergence steps.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Virtual Reality Environment for the Frazetta Art Museum
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Virtual reality is quickly becoming more and more accessible to everyone. Its introduction into the mobile market has made it spread everywhere. The COVID-19 pandemic affected museums worldwide, causing substantial declines in attendance and revenue. This paper presents a Virtual Reality (VR) project aimed at revitalizing the museum experience by virtualizing the Frazetta Art Museum. Utilizing Blender for 3D modeling, Unity as the game engine, and Oculus Quest 2 for deployment, the project enhances accessibility and engagement for a global audience. Interactive features include manipulable art frames, realistic door mechanics, an interactive whiteboard, dynamic snowfall effects, and immersive audio, all designed to provide a rich and participatory user experience. Our future extension to this project will include on integrating advanced 3D scanning, physics simulations, AI-driven virtual tour guides, and multi-user support to further enhance the virtual museum experience.

articleTitle: Source-based Smoke Characterization and Detection Using YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: In order to drastically minimize dangers to both life and property in interior situations, early fire detection is extremely important Optimizing YOLOv5 for real-time fire source detection and characterization-specifically, from cooking, cigarettes, and actual fire-is the main goal of this study. A high-resolution device prototype for capturing image, a creation of custom datasets of images related to fires, and an assessment of YOLOv5's accuracy, precision, and speed are among the objectives. By obtaining an average F1-score of 0.94 for cooking and cigarette sources and 0.92 for actual fire, the trained model showed excellent classification accuracy. The results of the confusion matrix show relatively little misclassification, confirming the system's dependability in differentiating between background items and potential fire hazards. Additionally, the model demonstrates its suitability for real-time applications with an average detection speed of 0.547 milliseconds. These results illustrate how YOLOv5 could boost fire detection systems by facilitating immediate and precise fire source identification, lowering false alarm rates, and promoting better safety protocols and risk reduction.

articleTitle: Automatic Question Generation From Handwritten Lecture Notes Using Trocr Text Recognition and T5 Language Processing
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: This research involves the creation and evaluation of a system that allows for text extraction and automatic question generation (AQG) using a T5 and TrOCR pipeline. With the use of a Raspberry Pi 5, web camera, and a touchscreen display, factoid- type questions are created from image captures of single-column handwritten notes that only contain textual information. The T5 large language model (LLM) used was finetuned using the Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD) for facilitating question generation. The system had a word error rate (WER) of 0.40, a ROUGE-1 score of 0.358, and a question validity rate of 68%. This research helps to promote the ease of creation of learning materials in learner education.

articleTitle: An Embedding Algorithm Based on Neighborhood Aggregation for Attribute Graphs
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Attribute graph embedding algorithms based on graph neural networks aggregate information about the neighborhood of a target node to update the embedding of the target node, i.e. neighborhood aggregation. The shallow network architecture of existing models limits the generalization ability of the models on large datasets, and the number of nodes increases exponentially with the number of graph neural network layers, resulting in gradient explosion and the need for faster model training methods. In addition, the multiple iteration process of neighborhood aggregation changes the original attribute information of the nodes, especially when the attributes of the target node and the attribute information of the neighborhood nodes are extremely different, which makes the target node attributes deviate significantly from the original attributes. Excessive neighborhood aggregation mixes different clustered nodes, causing all nodes to converge to the same embedding, resulting in excessive smoothing. In order to solve the above problems while considering the supervised learning of the model and the utility of neighborhood aggregation, this paper proposes a subgraph sampling method based on graph sampling for attribute graph data pre-processing, and an attribute graph embedding algorithm for improving neighborhood aggregation using an adaptive learning strategy.

articleTitle: Representative Community Detection Algorithms for Attribute-Free Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: In the field of network analysis, methods for identifying community structure often involve optimizing a specific objective function to achieve a single optimal allocation from network nodes to communities. However, in practice, we often encounter multiple division schemes with high quality scores that are close to the overall optimum. In fact, an accurate depiction of the community structure is more appropriately achieved by a series of high-quality division schemes rather than relying on a single optimal solution alone. However, such a collection of network divisions may be difficult to interpret, as its size may rapidly expand to hundreds or even thousands. To this end, this paper introduces an innovative strategy to reveal the diversity of network community structures more comprehensively and to provide a set of more globally-visioned delineation results by clustering similar network divisions and then selecting representative divisions from each cluster.

articleTitle: Image-Based Classification of Healthy and Infected Cacao Pods Using Google Teachable Machine
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Cacao cultivation is crucial for the global chocolate industry, yet it faces significant challenges from diseases such as Black Pod Rot and Pod Borer, which threaten yield and product quality. These issues are particularly pressing in the Philippines, where cacao production has grown steadily but remains vulnerable to these diseases. This study evaluates the effectiveness of Google Teachable Machine, a user-friendly webbased platform, in classifying healthy and diseased cacao pods. A dataset of 4,493 images [7]—comprising 3,344 healthy pods, 943 Black Pod Rot-infected pods, and 206 Pod Borer-infected pods—was used to train the machine learning model. Preprocessing steps included resizing all images to 224×224 pixels and normalizing pixel values to ensure consistent input quality. Transfer learning with MobileNet served as the backbone architecture, leveraging its lightweight and efficient design for image classification. The dataset was divided into training (85%) and testing (15%) sets to evaluate the model's performance on unseen data. Evaluation metrics included accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The model achieved an overall accuracy of 91.11%, with precision at 96.85%, recall at 93.61%, and an F1score of 95.20%, underscoring its robust performance in distinguishing healthy and infected cacao pods. Slight overfitting was observed after 35 epochs, reflected in an increase in validation loss, highlighting the need for dataset expansion and regularization techniques. Despite these limitations, the model demonstrated significant potential for early disease detection. Future work should focus on increasing dataset diversity, particularly for underrepresented diseases like Pod Borer. Integrating the trained model into mobile applications would enable real-time disease diagnosis in field conditions, offering farmers a practical, cost-effective solution for improving disease management and promoting sustainable cacao production.

articleTitle: Quantization of Tiny MLP-Mixer and Its Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: MLP-Mixer is a deep learning-based image classifier model that does not have any convolutional or self-attention mechanism, and is attracting attention for its competitiveness of accuracy and throughput against conventional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and state-of-the-art models such as Vision Transformer (ViT). This study proposes a quantization method for MLP-Mixer aimed at hardware circuit implementation, and evaluate its effectiveness through experiments. The results demonstrate that MLP-Mixer can be trained with low precision to a certain extent, and when represented using 4-bit and 8 -bit integers, its accuracy is comparable to that of a highprecision model that uses 32-bit floating-point numbers.

articleTitle: Parameter Free Countermeasure Against Adversarial Examples
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: In recent years, the increasing number of reported crimes in Japan has drawn attention to crime prevention sys-tems. Among these, intelligent security systems utilizing image classification neural networks (NNs) have been employed to enhance security by detecting suspicious individuals lingering for extended periods or identifying intruders in restricted areas. These systems use image classification NNs to perform tasks such as detecting individuals, estimating attributes like gender and age, and predicting movements from camera images. However, several attack methods targeting such image classification NNs used in these security systems have been reported. One of these is the use of adversarial examples (AEs), which are images intentionally perturbed with noise to cause misclassification by the NN. If such AEs appear in security camera footage, the system may fail to function correctly, making countermeasures essential. In this study, we propose an AE defense method using GIF conversion that can be applied to existing NNs. Additionally, we evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method through experimental validation.

articleTitle: Factor Contribution Evaluation for Sustainability Implementation in Post-Disaster Reconstruction Projects using Neural Network-based Sensitivity Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: The factor evaluation for sustainability implementation in post-disaster reconstruction projects was conducted using artificial neural network (ANN)-based sensitivity analysis. The current study involves the utilization of Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm (LMA) for the ANN model development. The findings demonstrated that the governing network structure is 10-3-1 utilizing input parameters (IP) including waste management (Sl), environmental impact management (S2), support of management (S3), construction cost (S4), public health and safety (S5), user security (S6), noise pollution (S7), energy consumption (S8), public services (S9), and recycling (S10). The results revealed that the governing model (GM) has a performance of correlation (R) = 0.99813 and Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 0.00110 and 0.4240/0, respectively. Moreover, a sensitivity analysis (SA) using Garson's algorithm (GA) reveals a trend of the relative value (RV) was observed to be construction cost > public services > support of management > user security > environmental impact management> noise pollution> public health and safety> energy consumption > recycling > waste management wherein the construction cost is the most influential parameter to the sustainability rating in post-disaster reconstruction projects (PDRP). The study shows how well ANN can detect the crucial elements that determine a project's sustainability rating in the post-disaster reconstruction projects.

articleTitle: Quadcopter Air Quality Monitoring and Evaluation System
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: The air we breathe is one of the basic human needs for survival, and since it cannot be seen by the naked eye, it is often ignored. However, air contains different pollutants that could cause problems to human health. This study aimed to monitor the air quality in certain areas with the advantage of the mobility of a drone. The device can monitor areas that were hard to access and did not have an air quality monitoring station. The data read by the sensors were displayed live using a mobile application. By following the Rapid Application Development (RAD) Model, the system's proven capabilities achieved the desired outcome. The Ozone sensor (MQ131) and the laser dust sensor (PM 2.5 Sensor) are connected to the R1 D1 WeMos, together with the ESP8266 that was integrated into the board of R1 D1 WeMos. The ESP8266 module allowed the data read by the sensors to be sent to ThingSpeak, the system's online database, from which the data were retrieved and displayed live on a mobile application created using the MIT App inventor. The demonstration of the working system was done by turning on the sensors first, so the MQ131 could calibrate to make sure that the data read by the sensors were accurate. The significant change in the measurements between the ground level and the air level monitoring was compared and evaluated.

articleTitle: Mitigating Bias in Home Maintenance Recommendations: A Fairness-Aware Approach Using Memory-Based Collaborative Filtering
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Recommendation systems, while beneficial, often perpetuate biases, leading to unfair outcomes. This study focuses on mitigating popularity and gender biases within a mobile application. Aiming to develop a fairness-aware system, the research utilizes the MovieLens 1M dataset, employing three approaches. First, a personalized recommendation algorithm was developed, combining collaborative filtering with cosine similarity and demographic filtering. Second, a fairness-aware re-ranking algorithm, Deterministic Greedy, was designed to balance item popularity and gender representation. Third, these algorithms were integrated into a prototype mobile application. Usability testing and unit testing confirmed the application's effectiveness and adherence to ISO 9126 guidelines. This research provides a practical solution for mitigating multiple biases, demonstrating the feasibility of creating more equitable and ethical artificial intelligence systems. The findings contribute to the broader discourse on fairness in artificial intelligence, offering a template for developing inclusive recommendation platforms.

articleTitle: Power Based Side-Channel Analysis for Lightweight Cipher Ltlbc
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Industry 5.0 requires security measures because of the threat of cyber attacks and data leaks from outside due to the communication of a variety of data. As a cryptographic technique for security measures, LTLBC, a low-latency lightweight cipher that can be used in industrial equipment at high speed, is attracting attention. On the other hand, the security of cryptographic circuits requires the tamper resistance against sidechannel analysis. So far, tamper resistance evaluation of LTLBC is insufficient. Therefore, this study proposes an evaluation method to verify the security of LTLBC against side-channel analysis. Experiments using a field programmable gate array show that the proposed method can be used to evaluate the tamper resistance of LTLBC against side-channel analysis using 1,400 waveforms.

articleTitle: A Study of Machine Learning Model's Performance for Load Forecasting Based on XAI Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Accurate load forecasting is crucial for efficient management, planning, and operation of modern power systems, especially in an era of increasing electrical demand driven by technological advancements and environmental changes. This paper explores the development of hybrid Transformer-based models to improve load forecasting accuracy by capturing shortterm fluctuations and long-term dependencies in energy demand. Three hybrid models were developed, the RNR-Transformer, the GRU-Transformer, and the LSTM-Transformer, and compared with traditional hybrid models such as LSTM-GRU and GRURNN. Transformer models outperformed standard RNN-based architectures, with an MSE of 0.0066 and a Symmetric Mean Absolute Percentage Error (sMAPE) of 15.09%, highlighting its ability to predict energy demand with higher accuracy. Feature importance analysis, using Random Forest, Permutation Importance, and SHAP, highlighted temperature as the most influential variable affecting demand, followed by solar radiation and humidity. The implications of these findings are significant in this field, as hybrid models can enhance the adaptability of load forecasting. These can be implemented in different geographical regions and market conditions, improving energy management, reducing operational costs, and facilitating the integration of renewable energy sources into power grids.

articleTitle: Enhancing Low-Resolution Images for FaceNet Facial Recognition Using GFPGAN on Raspberry Pi 5
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Throughout the years, significant advancements have been made in the field of photography and facial recognition technologies. And these technological advancements have become essential for numerous applications. However, traditional image enhancement algorithms often struggle to improve the image quality required for reliable feature extraction in facial recognition. In response, this study proposes the use of a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN), specifically GFPGAN (Generative Facial-Prior GAN), to enhance low-resolution images for facial recognition using FaceNET on Raspberry Pi 5. The system utilizes a Raspberry Pi V3 Camera Module to capture the images of participants at varying distances and angles. A total of 500 images underwent recognition, 250 of which were enhanced by GFPGAN. The system achieved an overall accuracy of 86.80% with GFPGAN-Assisted Facial Recognition, outperforming Standard Facial Recognition with an accuracy of 57.60 %. The results of the study emphasize the capability of GFPGAN in enhancing low-resolution images for facial recognition, which enables the development of facial recognition systems that can maintain high accuracy under suboptimal imaging conditions and the development of more dependable and secure applications that concern privacy and security.

articleTitle: Low Jerk Control of Active Suspension for Ride Comfort
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: This paper deals with the problem of improving the ride comfort of vehicles when the road surface changes stepwise. We show that the ride comfort problem can be expressed as the standard <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{2}$</tex> control framework. We consider using the jerk in the evaluation as well as the acceleration that is usually used for the ride comfort of vehicles. A controller synthesis method that simultaneously suppresses the acceleration and the jerk is proposed. The explicit use of the jerk in the evaluation causes some difficulties. We propose to modify the evaluation output to have physical and causal meaning to avoid the difficulties. With these modifications, we show that the problem can be reduced to a standard <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{2}$</tex> control framework, and a dynamic state feedback controller is derived. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by a numerical example.

articleTitle: The Vibration and Noise Simulation and Optimization of High-Speed Permanent Magnet Motor
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: High-speed permanent magnet motors are prone to generating vibration noise due to their elevated rotational speeds. Excessive vibration noise can compromise motor stability, potentially causing damage to the motor and surrounding equipment, while also contributing to environmental noise pollution. Electromagnetic vibration noise (E-NVH) simulation analysis provides a valuable tool for evaluating the motor's vibration and noise characteristics under various operating conditions, serving as a foundation for noise reduction and optimization. In this study, a 24-slot 2-pole (24S2P) permanent magnet motor is used as an example to perform vibration noise simulations. Structural parameters are subsequently optimized to achieve significant noise reduction.

articleTitle: Twin-Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient Algorithm for Active Suspensions Incorporating Preview Strategies
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: In the field of Active Suspension Control (ASC), traditional control algorithms often lack adaptability and require considerable time and effort for parameter tuning. Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies offer a promising solution to address these limitations. However, most Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) algorithms in ASC are based on passive, reactive responses, which will cause the decline in control performance when encountering transient road surface changes. Hence this study proposes a Preview information-based DRL (P-DRL) for ASC. First, the Twin-Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) algorithm is employed to train the neural controller, with a reward function defined according to the system's expected final state. Then, A new preview experience replay buffer is introduced to store system states at future time steps, and it is combined with the existing experience replay buffer to generate coupled predictive control states. Simulation results validate the proposed algorithm, showing a 70.29% improvement in spring acceleration.

articleTitle: Influence Analysis of Rotor Topologies on Power Density of PMSM Used in Large-Scale EMP
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Electro-hydrostatic direct drive system integrates servo motor, pump and actuator, which has the advantages of high integration, large power to weight ratio and high reliability, has been applied in aerospace, high-end robots, large underwater equipment and high-end construction machinery. Aiming at the problems of low power density and mismatch of high efficiency zone of motor pump, a high power density drive motor is designed to meet the high power density requirement of existing electrohydrostatic direct drive system of high-end construction machinery. The electromagnetic performance of the drive motor under different rotor topologies is calculated and analyzed. On this basis, the effect of permanent magnet size on motor performance is studied. The adaptive response surface method (ARSM) is used to optimize the motor, and the power density of the motor is improved.

articleTitle: Continuous Estimation of Joint Angle with Surface Electromyography (sEMG) and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: In this paper, we presented a novel attention-based convolutional neural networks (CNN)-long short-term memory (LSTM) models using surface electromyography (sEMG) signal to estimate continuous joint angle of upper limb. 7 subjects were recruited to participate in the experiment. Joint angles were generated using the simulation software-OpenSIM as the training label. Then, the model's performance was evaluated under different motions by using Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Cross Correlation (CC). Our study shows that the proposed model can achieve the excellent performance, with a good agreement with experimental values for all cases. After that, the prediction performance of the model was compared with and without the preprocessing of window approach. It is found that, using window approach leads to a reduction in RMSE of 4.7-7.2 deg and an improvement in CC of 1.7-3.8%. In conclusion, our proposed model has an accurate continuous estimation of hand movements, offering a promising solution for the human-machine interaction and cooperation.

articleTitle: Assessing Fatality in AI, ML, and NN Solutions for Critical-Safety Systems in Transportation, Industrial, and Construction Industries
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: This study explores the trend to apply artificial intelligent (AI), machine learning (ML), and neural network (NN) based solutions to safety-critical systems in transportation, industrial, and construction sectors of the industry. NN is introduced as subsets of AI and ML. The fatality rates for the three industrial sectors are presented as a reference for the expectation of AI, ML, and NN solutions in safety-critical systems. The reliability of such systems has to significantly improve and probability of fatality in such AI solutions to safety-critical systems should be hundred or thousand times or higher order of magnitude lower. Reliability standards and methods for AI solutions have been and are being developed to meet the stringent requirements.

articleTitle: Human-Like Behavior Decision Making in Autonomous Driving Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Autonomous driving is a key focus for future transportation systems, where decision-making in dynamic environments is critical. Current models have difficulty ensuring the safety of decision-making. To address this problem, a humanlike autonomous driving decision-making model is proposed, which incorporates driver style into the deep Q network (DQN) algorithm. First, by simulating different driving styles, the model can optimize decision-making, improve safety, and reduce collision rate. Then, the design of the reward function reflects the characteristics of the driver, and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{Q}$</tex> function weights of DQN are adjusted to consider goal achievement, speed maintenance, safe distance, and time efficiency in highway scenarios. Simulation experiments further verify its potential in optimizing highway driving decisions. And compared with the proximal policy optimization (PPO) algorithm, the proposed model reduces the collision rate by 6.33 % in aggressive driving scenarios.

articleTitle: Effect of Weather Conditions and Obstructions on Vehicle Model, Logo, and License Plate Recognition Systems Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Vehicle recognition systems are used in various sectors of our modern society. Environmental factors greatly affect the efficiency of these systems. This study aims to determine the effect of weather conditions such as direct sunlight, cloudy weather, and rain on a YOLO based system's ability to detect a vehicle's model, logo, and license plate.

articleTitle: Innovative Electrocardiogram Authentication System by Using Tailor-Made Compact Data Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Conventional authentication systems often rely on alphanumeric or graphical passwords, or token-based methods. The disadvantages of these systems include the risk of forgetfulness, loss, and theft. Biometric authentication which is a solution to these issues is quickly taking the place of traditional methods and becoming a ubiquitous part of daily life. The electrocardiogram (ECG) is one of the most recent traits considered for biometric purposes. A notable contribution of this work is the introduction of a novel ECG time-slicing technique that outperforms other ECG-based methods. By leveraging machine learning algorithms and tailor-made compact data learning techniques, this research presents a more robust, reliable biometric authentication system. Upon evaluation, the proposed system showed up to 95% identification accuracy when using the optimal machine learning model. These findings could lead to substantial advancements in network information security, with potential applications across various internet and mobile services.

articleTitle: Uav Detect, Track and Follow (DTF) of Non-Stationary Targets in Aerial Thermal Videos
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Evolution of portable Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) have rejuvenated the research on real-time target tracking in aerial systems. These devices are highly optimized in terms of volume, size, power, weight and are effectively employed in UAV based applications. Tracking a target can be broadly divided into two sub-categories: (a) Surveillance and Tracking of the target from a distance and (b) Track and Follow towards the target(e.g. medical and e-commerce deliveries), where the UAV has to intercept the target as closely as possible. Surveillance applications are extensively studied and successfully implemented in real-time. However, present day target follow applications rely completely on the GPS data for intercepting the target. In this work, we propose a novel convolutional neural network (CNN) based target follow in GPS denied environments. The proposed application presents novel challenges in real-time with changes in aspect ratio, target orientation, size of the target in the Field of View (FOV) and track loss. This is further exacerbated in case of thermal systems due to limited information and low thermal contrast ratios between foreground and background. In this work, we address the problem of target follow specifically in thermal videos. We deployed the proposed solution on a portable NVIDIA GPU integrated on a custom developed UAV. The algorithm proposed is successfully tested and validated and the results obtained demonstrate the efficiency of the algorithm for aerial thermal datasets.

articleTitle: A Swarm Fire-Fighting Robots Dynamic Control Model for Mine Fires
publicationTitle: 2025 17th International Conference on Computer and Automation Engineering (ICCAE)
abstract: Fire poses a significant threat to human activities and industrial production, particularly in large-scale industrial settings such as mining operations. This paper proposes a control model for swarm fire-fighting robots to mitigate the impacts and risks associated with fires. The proposed model can dynamically adjust the number of fire-fighting robots according to the severity of multiple fire points to efficiently fight fires in a cooperative manner. By adopting the model, more fire-fighting robots are allocated to severe fire points, while fewer robots are allocated for less critical fire points. The approach prevents uneven deployment, which could lead to out-of-control fires or unutilised resources.

articleTitle: Seismic Activated Circuit Breaker for Real-Time Monitoring and Contol Using GSM-Microcontroller Integration
